newsitem.title: USA: Talks to avert GM parts strike move slowly.
newsitem.headline: Talks to avert GM parts strike move slowly.

text.p: Negotiations to avert a potentially costly strike on Thursday at a General Motors Corp. catalytic converter plant in Wisconsin were moving slowly on Wednesday, a key union official said.

A strike at the Delphi Energy and Engine Management Systems plant in Oak Creek, Wis., near Milwaukee, would quickly shut down GM's North American assembly lines and would cut off some supplies to customers in Europe and Asia.
A 17-day strike earlier this year at two GM brake plants in Ohio idled 26 assembly plants and more than 175,000 workers, costing GM about $900 million.
About 870 members of UAW Local 1866 in Oak Creek have threatened to strike at 11:59 p.m. EDT Thursday unless bargainers reach a tentative agreement for a new local labor contract at the plant.
Major issues in the negotiations include staffing levels and other health and safety issues, subcontracting and long-term job security.
"It's slow," Local 1866 President Skip Dziedzic said of the talks. "The progress is minimal at this point in time."

He said he hoped that the plant, which never had a strike since it opened in 1974, would be able to continue production without a work stoppage, but the local labor talks with GM have dragged on for 11 months.
"There's still sufficient time to reach an agreement, but I thought we'd be further along at this point," Dziedzic said.

GM, which is already battling a seven-week strike over staffing levels at its Pontiac, Mich., truck plant, also faces Friday night strike deadlines at two other key parts plants, a foundry in Saginaw, Mich., and a metal stamping plant in Grand Rapids, Mich.

A strike by the 912 hourly workers the Saginaw plant would cut off supplies of pistons, piston rods and transmission parts for a number of GM vehicles. A walkout by the 2,346 hourly workers in Grand Rapids would would cut off supplies of stamped sheet-metal parts for a variety of cars and trucks.
Negotiations continued at those facilities Wednesday, with no major progress reported.
